purpose: Bounded MEPS 2024 event-family ledger connecting month-precision health events to round-level payment, health, work, and bill context plus a strict-window same-person R5/3 follow-up, without treating descriptive persistence or transition as event-specific recovery.

events.geography: United States; MEPS 2024 public-use person/event universe
events.date_precision: calendar-year event-family marker; first valid office event is month-precision and not necessarily the initiating need or first care contact
events.denominator: 14,181 people with a first valid office-event family and 134,506 source event records; person and event universes differ
events.method: Structured extraction from the retained MEPS 2024 bounded episode ledger joined by privacy-minimized person/event key and panel; weighted descriptive summaries retained without causal estimation
events.missingness: No event-specific need, amount owed, provider/coverage alternative, care choice, appeal, remedy, household payer, trust, action, switching, or exit is retained
events.exposure: First valid office-based event family is identified and ordered against the R4/2 reference-period endpoint month
events.alternatives_before_action: Provider, network, coverage, travel, payment, family, and service alternatives are not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Weighted self/family payment means range from about $38.80 in same-endpoint-month records to $65.41 in before-endpoint records; these are round/event-family context, not a bill amount for the displayed event
events.choice_or_response: Timing group and round context are observed; event-specific care continuation, delay, substitution, or foregoing is not observed
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Provider, insurer, household, and patient decision authority are not identified in the staged record
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Denial, prior-authorization, coverage, and bill context may appear in round fields, but no event-specific institutional decision or remedy is linked
events.immediate_outcome: Month-ordered health, employment, payment, and bill context is available around the office-event family
events.protected_outcome: Some later health and employment context is observed; no event-specific protected outcome is established
events.sacrificed_outcome: Payment, health, work, and bill pressures may coexist, but household sacrifice, unpaid care, food, housing, and debt response are not assigned to this event
events.cost_risk_transfer: Round-level payment and bill context can reveal material exposure while leaving the payer, alternative, and institutional burden allocation unknown
events.later_outcome: A strict R3/1–R4/2 event window is followed by same-person R5/3 health and employment measures; event-specific recovery, persistence cause, treatment continuity, trust, action, switching, and exit remain unknown
events.meaning_and_attribution: No event-linked fairness, blame, trust, or identity judgment is retained
events.public_or_collective_response: No complaint, appeal, organizing, political action, or collective response is linked
events.counterexample: A later improvement or worsening can reflect baseline selection, treatment, unrelated events, or reporting context; it is not automatically event recovery or failure
events.source_and_uncertainty: Retained MEPS 2024 bounded episode ledger; person/event linkage and weighted context are available, but the first observed event is not necessarily the triggering need and no raw respondent archive is retained

events.geography: United States; MEPS 2024 public-use person/event universe
events.date_precision: calendar-year event-family marker; first valid emergency-room event is month-precision and not necessarily the initiating need
events.denominator: 2,717 people with a first valid emergency-room event family and 3,962 source event records; timing groups are separately defined
events.method: Structured extraction from the retained MEPS 2024 bounded episode ledger joined by privacy-minimized person/event key and panel; weighted descriptive summaries retained without causal estimation
events.missingness: No event-specific severity, amount owed, alternative, care choice, appeal, remedy, household payer, trust, action, switching, or exit is retained
events.exposure: First valid emergency-room event family is identified and classified before, during, or after the R4/2 reference-period endpoint month
events.alternatives_before_action: Urgent-care, provider, coverage, transport, payment, family, and non-use alternatives are not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Weighted self/family payment means are about $90.58 after the endpoint month, $148.87 before it, and $104.23 in the same month; these are event-family context, not event-specific bills
events.choice_or_response: Timing and round context are observed; emergency-care choice, delay, substitution, and foregoing are not observed
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Emergency provider, insurer, household, and patient decision authority are not identified
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: No event-specific provider, insurer, billing, or appeal response is linked; round denial or care-delay fields remain context
events.immediate_outcome: Month-ordered health, employment, payment, and bill context is available around the emergency-room event family
events.protected_outcome: Some health and employment follow-up is observed; no event-specific protection or restoration is established
events.sacrificed_outcome: Payment and possible work/health burden are visible only as contextual measures; unpaid care, food, housing, and debt sacrifices remain unknown
events.cost_risk_transfer: Urgent health events may shift payment and time risk to people or families, but the ledger cannot identify who paid or what alternative was feasible
events.later_outcome: A strict R3/1–R4/2 event window is followed by same-person R5/3 health and employment measures; event-specific recovery, persistence cause, treatment continuity, trust, action, switching, and exit remain unknown
events.meaning_and_attribution: No event-linked fairness, blame, trust, or identity judgment is retained
events.public_or_collective_response: No complaint, appeal, organizing, political action, or collective response is linked
events.counterexample: The before/after timing contrast is subject to baseline selection and does not identify an emergency event effect or treatment failure
events.source_and_uncertainty: Retained MEPS 2024 bounded episode ledger; month-ordered person/event context is descriptive and does not supply a complete care or payment episode

events.geography: United States; MEPS 2024 public-use person/event universe
events.date_precision: calendar-year event-family marker; first valid inpatient event is month-precision and not necessarily the initiating need
events.denominator: 1,337 people with a first valid inpatient event family and 1,786 source event records; timing groups are separately defined
events.method: Structured extraction from the retained MEPS 2024 bounded episode ledger joined by privacy-minimized person/event key and panel; weighted descriptive summaries retained without causal estimation
events.missingness: No event-specific severity, amount owed, alternative, discharge choice, payment completion, appeal, remedy, household payer, trust, action, switching, or exit is retained
events.exposure: First valid inpatient event family is identified and classified before, during, or after the R4/2 reference-period endpoint month
events.alternatives_before_action: Hospital, coverage, transport, caregiving, payment, and non-use alternatives are not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Weighted self/family payment means are about $796.48 after the endpoint month, $838.09 before it, and $597.26 in the same month; these are event-family context, not event-specific bills
events.choice_or_response: Timing and round context are observed; inpatient admission, discharge, substitution, caregiving, and payment choices are not observed
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Hospital, insurer, household, caregiver, and patient decision authority are not identified
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: No event-specific hospital, insurer, billing, discharge, or appeal response is linked
events.immediate_outcome: Month-ordered health, employment, payment, and bill context is available around the inpatient event family
events.protected_outcome: Some health and employment follow-up is observed; no event-specific protection, treatment continuity, or recovery is established
events.sacrificed_outcome: Payment and possible work/health burden are visible only as contextual measures; caregiving, food, housing, and debt sacrifices remain unknown
events.cost_risk_transfer: Inpatient events can shift payment, time, and caregiving risk to households, but the ledger does not identify the payer, alternative, or institutional remedy
events.later_outcome: A strict R3/1–R4/2 event window is followed by same-person R5/3 health and employment measures; event-specific recovery, persistence cause, treatment continuity, trust, action, switching, and exit remain unknown
events.meaning_and_attribution: No event-linked fairness, blame, trust, or identity judgment is retained
events.public_or_collective_response: No complaint, appeal, organizing, political action, or collective response is linked
events.counterexample: Timing groups differ in baseline health and employment; follow-up differences cannot be treated as an inpatient event effect or recovery estimate
events.source_and_uncertainty: Retained MEPS 2024 bounded episode ledger; month-ordered person/event context is descriptive and does not supply a complete hospitalization, household, or remedy episode

arrows.to: month-ordered payment, health, work, and bill context
arrows.evidence: The retained ledger joins first valid event-family rows by privacy-minimized person/event key and classifies event month relative to the R4/2 endpoint month
arrows.counterexample: The first observed event is not necessarily the initiating need, first contact, or causal trigger
arrows.remaining_gap: Exact need, bill, event severity, payer, and claim-level timing

arrows.to: later health, employment, and bill context
arrows.evidence: The strict R3/1–R4/2 event-window screen carries the same people to R5/3 and records fair/poor-health resolution or onset, health worsening, nonemployment resolution or onset, and status change for office, ER, and inpatient event families
arrows.counterexample: These are weighted descriptive transitions, not causal effects or verified recovery: baseline severity, unrelated events, treatment, attrition, and reporting differences can generate the contrasts
arrows.remaining_gap: Event-specific outcome, treatment continuity, household adaptation, remedy, and design-based causal comparison

arrows.to: household choice, institutional remedy, trust, action, or exit
arrows.evidence: The retained event ledger has no usable alternatives, event-specific choice, provider/insurer response, verified remedy, meaning, action, switching, non-use, or exit fields
arrows.counterexample: Person-level event linkage does not identify the household payer, caregiver, decision-maker, or feasible alternative
arrows.remaining_gap: Need/amount, alternatives, chosen/delayed care, payment completion, appeal/correction, household security, trust, action, and exit

boundary: This ledger formalizes MEPS 2024 as a person-linked, month-ordered health-event context scaffold with a strict-window same-person R5/3 follow-up. It establishes descriptive later health/work transitions, not a health-cost causal effect, event-specific household burden, remedy, verified recovery, trust, action, switching, or exit.
storage_boundary: No raw MEPS respondent or event archive is retained in this artifact; only bounded aggregate event-family fields, denominators, timing, uncertainty, and open arrows from the committed local ledger are represented.
